clue.text: Giant company (American) absorbing poor trading figure

indicators.note: absorbing means the company-and-American pair takes the trading figure into its middle

parts.note: US stands for American, as in the United States
a poor result in trading is a loss

explanation.surface: A big American firm swallows a poor set of trading results.
explanation.definitionFit: A colossus is a person or thing of enormous size, a giant.

clue.text: Get the better of the market after disaster's headed off

indicators.note: after places the market word behind the trimmed disaster word
headed off means the first letter of the disaster word is cut away

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat, a disaster
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: A trader recovers from a calamity to beat the market.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsmart someone is to outwit them, getting the better of them by cleverness.

clue.text: Street entertainer giving out notes from a barrel?

definitions.text: Street entertainer giving out notes from a barrel?

parts.words: Street entertainer giving out notes from a barrel?
parts.note: a busker cranking a barrel organ, whose music comes from a pinned barrel; the surface tempts thoughts of money handed out

explanation.surface: A busker hands out banknotes from a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A street musician who plays a barrel organ by turning a handle is the classic street entertainer of this name.

clue.text: It's evident in understated translation, perhaps

indicators.note: evident in means the first word can be seen sitting inside the understated word

parts.note: something understated is subtle
the word it, with the 's acting as a joining is

explanation.surface: A remark on how a quiet translation shows its point.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtitles on a foreign film are usually a translation of the dialogue, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Student of the sun taking in carbon and hydrogen

indicators.note: taking in means the sun word absorbs the two chemical symbols

parts.note: solar means of the sun
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A solar physicist studies how the sun absorbs carbon and hydrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or a student holding a scholarship.

clue.text: A sign American sailor is first to accept introduction of uniform

indicators.note: is first puts the sailor word ahead of the American word
to accept means the sailor word takes a letter into it

parts.note: tar is a traditional word for a sailor

indicators.note: introduction of picks the opening letter of uniform

explanation.surface: An American sailor is the first to put on a new uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the Bull, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Dreadful person, bad under pressure

indicators.note: under puts the bad word below the pressure letter in this down entry

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
ill can mean bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: An awful person behaves worse when under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Pill is informal slang for a tiresome, disagreeable person.

clue.text: Call, being upset about fire in the sky

indicators.note: about means the reversed call word goes around the fire word
being upset means the call word is turned upside down, read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: to name something is to call it
a pyre is a pile of wood set on fire, a bonfire

explanation.surface: Someone shouts in distress at a fire blazing across the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The empyrean is the highest heaven, poetically the sky or firmament.

clue.text: Reform movement curtailed Christmas breaks

indicators.note: breaks means the letters are smashed up and reassembled
curtailed means the last letter of Christmas is cut off

explanation.surface: A shortened Christmas holiday as a reform of the festive breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' drops the final S of Christmas to leave CHRISTMA, and 'breaks' rearranges those letters. Chartism was a 19th-century British working-class movement for parliamentary reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartism was the 1830s-40s British movement campaigning for electoral reform under the People's Charter.

clue.text: Firearms brought back for men

indicators.note: brought back means the firearms word is read in reverse

parts.note: gats is slang for guns

explanation.surface: Guns are returned for the men.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or stag event is restricted to men only.

clue.text: It's not an original view of sporting activity

definitions.text: It's not an original view of sporting activity

parts.words: It's not an original view of sporting activity
parts.note: on television, a repeated showing of a moment from a match, seen a second time rather than live

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone's take on sport lacks originality.
explanation.definitionFit: A televised repeat of a piece of play, often slowed down, is a second viewing of sport rather than the original.

clue.text: Good starting-point for race in icy location?

definitions.text: Good starting-point for race in icy location?

parts.words: Good starting-point for race in icy location?
parts.note: in motor racing, the front spot on the starting grid; whimsically read as a place near the North or South Pole

explanation.surface: Advice on where to start a race held somewhere frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: The front place on a motor-racing grid is the best starting spot, while the question mark invites a polar reading.

clue.text: Came upon Tom stifling expression of disgust

indicators.note: stifling means the tom word smothers the exclamation inside it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone happens on a tomcat and suppresses a cry of revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: To have caught someone is to have come upon them, as in caught red-handed.

clue.text: Bales out at sea for sure

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor is definitely baling water out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means certain or unqualified, so something stated for sure is absolute.

clue.text: Town's blemishes reported on the radio

indicators.note: reported on the radio means the word is heard spoken rather than seen

parts.note: stains are marks or blemishes

explanation.surface: Radio news reports a town's blemished reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Staines is a town in Surrey, west of London; 'Town's' is the definition plus a joining 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Staines-upon-Thames is a town in Surrey near Heathrow.

clue.text: Shoes are cast here perhaps

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Shoes kicked off on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges SHOES ARE, and the whole clue also describes the beach where people throw off their shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach by the sea is a place where shoes might be thrown off.

clue.text: Best chap going to University that's ideal

indicators.note: going to means the best and chap words follow on after the university letter

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks
Ian is a typical man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: The top man heads off to university, which is perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian means idealistic or perfect, like the imagined island of Utopia.

clue.text: Metal soldiers — set seen in castle

parts.note: tin is a metal
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers
to gel is to set, as jelly does

explanation.surface: Toy tin soldiers are set out in a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tintagel is a castle in Cornwall linked with King Arthur.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintagel Castle in Cornwall is famed in Arthurian legend.

clue.text: Doctor that's not at first in outstanding environment

indicators.note: in means the doctor, that's and not pieces sit inside the outstanding word

parts.note: ace means excellent or outstanding
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of not

explanation.surface: A doctor who isn't at first in an excellent setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambience is the atmosphere or character of a place, its environment.

clue.text: Island one regularly visited avoids a police search

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

indicators.note: avoids means the place word does without the letter a

parts.note: a haunt is a place one visits regularly
the letter itself

explanation.surface: An islander who keeps visiting dodges a police search.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhunt is an organised search, typically by police, for a person.

clue.text: A rebel rejected target in university circles

parts.note: Jack Cade led a 1450 rebellion in England

indicators.note: rejected means the target word is sent back the way it came

parts.note: an aim is a target

explanation.surface: A rebel turns his back on a target in academic circles.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the Kentish revolt of 1450 against Henry VI's government.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholarship.

clue.text: Arrangement of numbers: dull run ending with nine

parts.note: mat or matt means dull, without shine
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A tedious series of figures ends with a nine.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a matrix is a rectangular array of numbers.

clue.text: New article certainly backtracked about British battle

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means the reversed certainly word goes around the British letter
backtracked means the certainly word is read in reverse

parts.note: yes means certainly

explanation.surface: A new article definitely retracted its account of a British battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Naseby, in Northamptonshire, was the decisive 1645 battle of the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Naseby in 1645 was a key Parliamentarian victory in the English Civil War.

clue.text: How cards in one suit are arranged, to be frank

definitions.text: How cards in one suit are arranged
definitions.meaning: playing cards of the red suit with the symbol of love, laid next to one another
frank means candid and intimate, as in an open conversation

explanation.surface: A card player sorting a suit while speaking honestly.
explanation.definitionFit: A candid, intimate talk is described with this phrase, and cards of that suit placed side by side match it literally.

clue.text: Colleague not initially friendly?

indicators.note: not initially means the friendly word loses its opening letter

parts.note: pally is informal for friendly

explanation.surface: A coworker who may not be friendly from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a partner or associate, someone working on your side.

clue.text: One's supported by a part of Scotland

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is a joining is
something supported by another sits on it, giving the word on

explanation.surface: One person is held up by part of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, famous for its abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Tract's about line taken by one belief system

indicators.note: about means the tract word is put around the line and one pieces

parts.note: a tract of land is a region; the 's is a joining is

indicators.note: taken by means the line letter is followed by the one letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A religious tract on a line held by one creed.
explanation.definitionFit: A religion is a system of faith and worship, a belief system.

clue.text: Accomplished story's celebrated, nothing less

parts.note: a tale is a story; the 's is a joining is

indicators.note: less means the celebrated word is without the nothing letter

parts.note: noted means famous or celebrated
O represents nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A story is famous, nothing less.
explanation.definitionFit: Talented means gifted or skilled, which is to say accomplished.
